added_lines: . at fatima our lady promised that if we did what she asked there would be peace in the world and that many souls would be saved. unfolding the word: what mark’s gospel says about discipleship. an invitation to our family of parishes why not join us on thursdays 5th 12th 19th and 26th november in the parish room in holy cross church, mahon from 7.30 pm to 9.00 pm. an opportunity to come together and spend some time reading and discussing the scriptures, followed by prayer. everyone is most welcome and we even have a cuppa and chat afterwards as well!today we celebrate the community of faith, being in communion with all the saints, a day of both thanksgiving and vision. thanksgiving because of the example and inspiration of the saints, who have come to maturity, to the measure of the full stature of christ. (eph 4:13). vision because our gospel today describes the path we must take to make the same journey home to god. if we wish to join the saints both now and into eternity, we must make our own the “mission statement” of jesus, which is the sermon on the mount and especially the opening invitation to true happiness. prayer jesus you are our teacher within and today we ask your help. just as you have brought our brothers and sisters to full maturity in you, so also guide us and be with us as we walk your way. by your grace, may we too be counted among saints in the present moment and in the life to come.• first reading (revelation 7:2–4, 9–14) john sees a vast, uncountable multitude from every nation, race, and tongue, robed in white and standing before the throne and the lamb. these are the ones who have passed through trials and washed their robes clean in the blood of christ. second reading (1 john 3:1–3) st. john reminds believers of their present identity as children of god, noting that while what we shall be has not yet been fully revealed, we will be like him when we see him as he is. gospel (matthew 5:1–12a) the beatitudes from the sermon on the mount. jesus proclaims true blessing not in worldly power, but in spiritual poverty, meekness, mourning, hunger for righteousness, mercy, purity of heart, peacemaking, and endurance of persecution. the blessings in the beatitudes are primarily future blessings, but there can be an anticipation of the blessings in the present. at /f_irst reading some beatitudes may seem to describe circumstances that you would like to avoid at all costs. read them slowly. stay with each one for a while. let yourself get a sense of the paradox involved in each one. perhaps you have had an experience of a deeper and more authentic life, a blessing, when… 1. you were poor - you knew your need of god 2. you mourned – could feel for others 3. you were meek – not emotionally out of control 4. you hungered and thirsted for some cause 5. you were merciful rather than vengeful 6. you were pure in heart – a person of integrity, whose actions and intentions correspond 7. you were a peacemaker 8. you were persecuted because you stood for something prayer all-holy god, you call your people to holiness. as we keep the festival of your saints, give us their meekness and poverty of spirit, a thirst for righteousness, and purity of heart. may we share with them the richness of your kingdom and be clothed in the glory you bestow. remembering – as we move into the month of november, we will lovingly remember our loved ones who have died. 107 funeral masses have been celebrated across st. michael’s and holy cross churches since this time last year. 70 funeral masses have been celebrated in st. michael’s and 37 in holy cross church since the start of november last year. these details give us a sense of the strength of both parishes to prayerfully support one another at the most difficult of times. at each of these masses, there is a deep sense of the consoling presence of god and trust in the ultimate power of the risen jesus who ‘defeats death forever’. this sense runs very deep and is much more than just sharing our sympathies. it’s our prayer to accompany those who have died into the eternal presence of god and back into arms of their own deceased family members and loved ones. so, when we gather during this coming week for the remembrance mass, we will be praying, consoling and strengthening the heartbroken. while this is a sad time, it’s also a beautiful time and that is how we approach november, in hope and new life. may all those who have died now rest in the peace of the lord and may we remember them lovingly. may they rest in peace. - mon - wed. 9.00am - 12. 30pm we celebrate today the feast of all saints, not jus t the canonized, but all those people who have been faithful witnesses to the love of god by living out the message of the gospel during their life. we trust that our loved ones, relations and friends are among those who are now enjoying the glory and happiness of being face to face with god. the saints we celeb rate were men and women like us. perhaps we may sometimes think of our departed loved ones as being dead and gone. but our faith helps us to believe that they are alive now more than ever, bec ause they are now fully alive in god. the life they now enjoy can no longer be touched by sickness, su ffering, sin, or death. we thank god for all those whom he has already welcomed to heaven. during november we pray especially for those who are still being purified in purgatory knowing that our prayers can help them. the second reading from the first leʃer of st john, reminds us of the great love of god who already has chosen to call us his children. “what we are to be in the future has not yet been r evealed; all we know is, that when it is revealed, we will be like him, because we will see him as he is." the beatitudes in today’s gospel, propose to us a way of life, inviting us to be poor in spirit, that is relying on god to help us through life, to identify with the meek, those who mourn, and those who hunger and thirst after justice. they challenge us to be compassionate people, to be men and women who are in heart, and to become peacemakers in our deal ings with one another, in our families and in society at large, even when this entails ridicule and persecution. we pray for faith and courage to walk this journey. the saints encourage us in ourd ay-to-day struggles because like us they also endur ed struggles. our faith assures us that all who respond to the lord’s invitation to live the life of the beatitudes will one day hear those welcoming and consoling words, "well 'have life and have it all in its fullness'. 1 hour per week for 6 weeks. 2 small groups of 6 participants each. wednesday (men) thursdays (women) initial contact: fr alan o’leary pp or any priest in the mount jesus teaches us that if we live ac- cording to the beatitudes, we will live a happy christian life. the beatitudes fulfil god’s promises made to abraham and his descendants and describe the rewards that will be o urs as loyal followers of christ. blessed are the poor in spirit, for theirs is the k ingdom of heaven. blessed are they who mourn, for they will be comforted. blessed are the meek, for they will inherit the land. blessed are they who hunger and thirst for righteousness, for they will be satisfied. blessed are the merciful, for they will be shown me rcy. blessed are the clean in heart, for they will see god. blessed are the peacemakers, for they will be called children of god. blessed are they who are persecuted for the sake of righteousness, for theirs is the kingdom of heaven . prayer for vocations loving god, at baptism you have gifted each of us with a call to serve you and all people in everything we do. give us the strength to share your message of love, justice, hope and peace in every part of our diocese of cork and ross. we ask you lord, for the gift of new vocations to priesthood in our diocese. in your fatherly care, accompany those who are seeking to know your will for them. inspire those you invite to serve as priests and fill them with the courage to answer that call. throu gh christ our lord, amen. ballincollig

ate other people are, by visiting people in hospital, working with the vincent de paul society and visiting people in prison. yes all of these expressions of keeping t hese commandments happen in this family of parishes. so today let us thank god, that so many people observe loving god, with all their hearts, souls, and mind and loving their neighbours. blessing of the graves sunday 1st november kilquane -
